final_message:
I wrote the NIF issue memorandum (about 6,900 words). It passed the docx validator and opens cleanly when parsed back. Its main findings: the NIF's $613,470 total is $448,202 more than its own three categories add up to ($165,268). On top of that, all seven "knowing employment" counts rest on a 10-business-day deadline ICE counted wrong (the March 22 response was on time). Three charges are wrong on the facts (Reyes-Montoya, Gutierrez-Padilla, Coldwater), and 16–19 counts are technical errors that 8 U.S.C. § 1324a(b)(6) says cannot be fined without a chance to correct them. With the clear errors fixed, exposure is roughly $80,000; if the technical-error and good-faith arguments win, it is about $3,700–$33,000. The memo recommends filing the hearing request on July 12, 2024 (it is dated that day), sending it to the ICE office and to OCAHO, and asking for settlement talks in the same letter.

Several points rest on my own legal knowledge rather than the documents, and the memo flags them for checking before any filing. These are the 2024 penalty maximums (about $2,789 per paperwork violation and $5,579 for a first knowing-hire offense), the Form I-9 edition dates, and the OCAHO statute-of-limitations case cited. The record also has gaps: the Notice of Suspect Documents itself and the original I-9s were not in the file, and the internal spreadsheet lists only 200 of the 347 employees.
